final_message:
I'll look at the failing test and how items are listed so using the last of something drops it from GET /items.The new test expects a used-up item to leave the list, while an older store test still expects it to stay at quantity zero. I'll read both and see how listing works.Using the last of an item still leaves it in the list at quantity zero. I'll drop it once the quantity hits zero, and update the store test that still expects the old behavior.Using the last of an item now removes it from the household list. `GET /items` no longer includes it, and anything with some left still shows.

`Store.use` drops the item when its quantity reaches zero. `Store.items` only returns items with a quantity above zero, which is what `GET /items` and the expiring list both use. Buying that item again starts a new entry, so the old expiry date does not carry over.

`test_used_up_item_stays_listed` still expected a used-up item to remain at quantity zero. That test is now `test_used_up_item_leaves_the_list`.

`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` — 13 tests, all passed.
